steps.say: The Sales Analysis tab analyses sales. This video shows one way to get sales in: pasting the results of a sales search on Manitoba Assessment Online, which anyone with an M A O subscription can do.

Sign in to M A O as a subscriber and open the sales search. Pick the municipality, here the R M of Springfield, and the sale type group, here residential bare land. A tip: set a minimum sale amount of a hundred dollars or so. That keeps nominal, non-arm's-length transfers, like one-dollar sales, out of your results. Then Search.
M A O lists the matching sales a page at a time. Select the results table, including the header row, and copy it.
Back in Parcel Search, open Upload a C S V or Paste Sales from M A O, and click Paste data.

Paste the table into the box. The columns are the ones M A O gives you: sale date, consideration, municipality, roll number, street address, legal description and primary property. Roll number and municipality are the two the tool needs to find each parcel.

Press Load sales. Each sale is matched to its parcel and plotted. The status line reports how many were placed, any duplicates merged, and any roll not yet on the parcel map, which is shown at an approximate location.
From here the pasted sales go through the same filters as any other sales: date presets, assessment class and structure type, vacant or improved, and the additional filters.

If a search runs to several pages, copy each page into one Excel sheet, keeping a single header row, and save it as a C S V. Upload sales C S V loads that file into this same tool, and Recent brings back earlier pastes and uploads without copying them again.
The grid, the comp stars, the exclusion reasons and the Charts window all work on pasted sales the same way.
